QF.id: AIFM CIII AIFs in India and Suitability_6

question.text: Mr. Karthik Raghavan compares Satpura Market-Neutral Fund (Cat III AIF) to a large-cap equity mutual fund. Which statement is TRUE per Table 4.3 of the chapter?

answer.text: Cat III AIF minimum investment is INR 1 crore; mutual fund minimum is INR 500 or scheme-specified
Mutual funds can use leverage whereas Cat III AIFs cannot
Mutual funds have a maximum of 1,000 investors, same as Cat III AIFs
Both mutual funds and Cat III AIFs issue units through a public issue process

explanation.text: The Logic: Table 4.3: MF minimum investment is INR 500 (or scheme-specified); Cat III minimum is INR 1 crore (INR 25 lakh for AIF employees). MFs cannot leverage; Cat III CAN. MFs have no investor cap; Cat III is capped at 1,000. MFs issue via public issue; Cat III via private placement. The Trap: Option B inverts leverage permission. Option C wrongly puts a 1,000-investor cap on MFs. Option D wrongly puts public issue on Cat III — Cat III is private placement only. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C (All-Cat) covers the full MF-vs-AIF comparison. XIX-E narrows to Cat III vs MF. The private-placement-vs-public-issue distinction recurs in XXI-B (PMS) comparisons too.
